name: E. coli Heat Shock Response
description: "description": "This detailed Mermaid flowchart illustrates the Heat Shock Response (HSR) in *Escherichia coli*. It begins with various triggers such as heat stress, protonophores, or other environmental stresses, all leading to protein misfolding. These misfolded proteins sequester the DnaK-DnaJ-GrpE chaperone system, which normally targets the sigma factor RpoH (sigma32) for degradation by FtsH protease. With chaperones occupied, RpoH is released and accumulates. Increased RpoH, in conjunction with high cellular ATP levels, drives the transcription of heat shock genes. These genes encode chaperones (e.g., DnaK, GroEL) and proteases (e.g., FtsH, Lon) that refold misfolded proteins and degrade irreversibly aggregated ones, respectively. This process restores proteostasis, a state that ultimately leads to the re-engagement of chaperones with RpoH, targeting it for degradation and terminating the stress response, ensuring cellular survival and stress tolerance.",
